summary.intent: Run the GSD manager to discuss and plan phases 42-44 of the cipher-box project, covering three security/durability bug fixes: API unpin ownership enforcement, FUSE write durability, and IPNS conflict handling.
summary.outcome: Successfully discussed all three phases (42, 43, 44) producing CONTEXT.md and DISCUSSION-LOG.md for each, and completed planning for phase 42 (API unpin integrity) after recovering from a mid-run planner agent failure and repeated git signing issues.

repo: The unpin endpoint (POST /ipfs/unpin) accepts any JWT and passes the CID directly to Kubo pin/rm with no ownership check — any account holder can destroy another user's pinned content.

Kubo runs with the 'server' profile (docker/docker-compose.staging.yml:62-72) which disables local-network discovery but keeps full public DHT participation on swarm port 4001 — all pinned CIDs are harvestable by DHT crawlers.

Writable-share saves drop prunedCids without unpinning (shared-write.ts:450), so there is no legitimate cross-user unpin path — only the race/retry and the dedup-compensation path reach the no-row case.
BYO-IPFS delete flows do not call provider.unpin; the advisory unpin for bring-your-own nodes is entirely unwired.
FUSE release writes a temp file to disk but can be lost before the remote commit is acknowledged, creating a data-loss window on crash.
IPNS write auth is cryptographic (documented in .planning/notes/ipns-write-auth-is-cryptographic.md), constraining conflict-handling options.
The .planning/ and .claude/ directories were not in .prettierignore, causing prettier to mangle markdown tables (splitting regex pipes into table columns).
Git commit signing via 1Password intermittently requires the 1Password GUI to be unlocked; dangerouslyDisableSandbox is needed to unblock the signing prompt.

code.finding: Upload-compensation path fires a global pin/rm on a CID that content-addressed dedup may share with another user — a non-malicious path to the same cross-tenant unpin bug.

Kubo v0.40 runs with the 'server' profile and swarm port 4001 exposed publicly (tcp+udp). Server profile only disables LAN discovery; full public DHT participation is retained, so provider records for every pinned CID are broadcast.
Web client unpin calls use .catch(logger.warn) — errors are silently swallowed, so a 403 response would appear as a warn-log spike rather than a client-visible failure.

workflow: When a planner agent dies mid-run, partial PLAN.md files are left on disk and a completion agent can be spawned against the specific incomplete files rather than replanning from scratch.
Decision coverage gate (13/13 decisions, all items covered) should be run before committing plan files to catch gaps introduced by manual edits.
The 'silent 2XX + audit log' pattern (warn + metric on cross-user CID attempts, uniform response to avoid existence oracle) is the preferred unpin integrity design over a loud 403.
Transactional delete with a pending_unpins outbox and a per-CID advisory lock (Postgres advisory xact lock on hash(cid)) closes the dedup concurrency race without requiring a reconciliation job.
A read-only pin ls diff report (detect orphans, don't auto-GC) is sufficient for historical drift visibility without the footgun of destroying pins the relay path didn't create.

friction: Git commits silently failed to land multiple times (HEAD unchanged after commit) due to 1Password signing prompts being blocked in the sandboxed environment — required dangerouslyDisableSandbox to resolve.
Session limit hit mid-discussion of phase 42, interrupting the flow and requiring the user to re-send the last message.
Prettier was not ignoring .planning/ files, causing it to mangle regex pipes in markdown table cells — discovered only after a plan file was written and committed.
The planner agent died partway through phase 42, leaving three incomplete PLAN.md files that required a separate completion agent pass.
The assistant repeatedly presented AskUserQuestion menus instead of directly answering the user's explicit questions, requiring the user to call this out ('you did not answer my question').
STATE.md update was missing from the phase 44 initial commit and had to be added in a follow-up commit.
open_items: Wire provider.unpin into BYO-IPFS delete flows — deferred out of phase 42 scope.
Implement read-only pin ls drift report (pins not in pinned_cids ∪ pending_unpins) for historical orphan detection — deferred as defense-in-depth, not load-bearing.
Phase 43 (FUSE write durability) and Phase 44 (IPNS conflict handling) are discussed but not yet planned — planning was not initiated for either in this session.
Verify whether the per-CID advisory lock approach fully closes the dedup concurrency race under high-throughput concurrent deletes — noted as an assumption in the plan, not validated.
